main_text.p: Quinĉti & minæ eò spectant, ut homo in cruce fixus ustulctur fumo. Alexander etiam Imperator quempiam qui fumum vendiderat, quasi compari pœnâ affecturus, ad stipitem ligari præcepit, & fumo apposito quem ex stipulis & humidis lignis fieri jusserat, necavit, præcone dicente, Fumo punitur qui vendidit fumum1. Atque in Martyribus nostris hoc genus crebrum. Acta vetera de Pionio: Confixus clavis in cruce, aggestis lignis, flamâ combustus est. Nec aliter Polycarpus mortuus, antistes Smyrnæorum, ipsi in epistolâ2: Μιχαὴλ δ' ἀυτὸν ἠμὶ προαπολιπὼν, ἀπιὼν... ἐρπὶ τὸν πῦρ ...
1 Lampr. in Alex. 2 Apud Eusch. lib. IV. c. XV.

page.notes: Greek passage and the marginal note "Aut flamâ" at left, and the note of the first line of the paragraph, are only partly legible; Greek letters reproduced approximately. The final paragraph "Cum parārent eum cruci suffigere, dixit, Relinquite me sic. qui enim dedit exspectare ignem, dabit" continues beyond the visible text and is set in italic with the last word "dabit" at the right margin.
